_note: DEC-2026-014 replaces the misleading total-emitted-JavaScript ceiling with hard runtime-specific shared, largest-asset, and representative-route initial-JavaScript budgets. DEC-2026-015 applies the same reasoning to CSS: authored bytes across app/ are a sum of seven stylesheets rather than any page's payload, so they are a non-blocking trend and the enforced CSS ceilings are the per-build staticAssets ones. Both totals stay visible against a reference build. Byte values are uncompressed build output; user-centric targets remain below.

network._note: C9 raised the connected route ceilings by 4,153 bytes on 2026-09-05, measured against the build that converted the proposal, team, saved/offer, organization-inbox and notification page families to server authority. The increase is the typed command gateways the RuntimeProvider composes for those nine families; every connected page component itself is loaded on demand and stays out of this chunk. The demo ceilings guard the public static export and were not raised -- they fell by 4,761 bytes in the same change.
